payload.message: Reading about neural nets from scratch

lesson.title: A neural net from scratch
lesson.overview: We'll build a neural network with nothing but NumPy and teach it XOR. First the data, then random weights, a forward pass that makes a guess, backprop that gives each weight its share of the error, and a loop that trains it. At the end it answers 0 1 1 0 on its own.

primer.title: XOR
primer.body: 1 when exactly one input is 1. No single straight line separates its 1s from its 0s.

primer.title: Matrix multiply
primer.body: X @ W1 computes every hidden neuron's weighted sum, for all four examples at once.

primer.title: Sigmoid
primer.body: Squashes any number into 0..1. Its slope is σ(z)·(1 − σ(z)), which backprop reuses.

primer.title: Chain rule
primer.body: How a weight moves the loss: multiply the slopes along the path from that weight to the loss.
primer.diagramPrompt: The chain rule through a 2-4-1 network

primer.title: Gradient descent
primer.body: Step each weight a little against its gradient. Repeat, and the loss falls.

payload.title: Why the weights start random
payload.body: Two neurons with the same weights compute the same thing and get the same update. Random starts let each learn its own.

payload.caption: Two inputs, four hidden neurons, one output. Every line is one weight the loop learns.

payload.title: Why times 0.5
payload.body: Small starting weights keep sigmoid in its steep middle, where the gradients are big enough to learn fast.

payload.title: Hint
payload.body: W1 maps 2 inputs to 4 hidden neurons, so it's 2×4. W2 maps 4 to 1.

payload.title: Forward pass
payload.what: Sigmoid, and a forward pass from inputs to a guess
payload.why: Each layer is a weighted sum squashed by sigmoid. Two layers turn the inputs into a guess between 0 and 1.

payload.title: What forward computes
payload.body: Each hidden neuron takes a weighted sum of the inputs, squashed into 0..1 by sigmoid. W2 does it again to make one guess.

payload.caption: Two inputs, four hidden neurons, one output. Every line is one weight the loop learns.

payload.title: Sigmoid or ReLU?
payload.body: Both work. Sigmoid keeps outputs in 0..1 like XOR's answers, and its slope σ(1 − σ) keeps backprop to one line.

payload.caption: Type this here

payload.title: Hint
payload.body: forward returns h as well: backward needs it.

payload.title: Backprop
payload.instructions: Add backward. It returns one gradient per weight.
payload.what: A gradient for every weight, with the chain rule
payload.why: The chain rule passes the error back one layer at a time, so every weight learns its share of the blame.

payload.title: The chain rule, in this code
payload.body: out depends on h, h on W1. Multiply the slopes along that path: d_out is error × σ′, and d_h carries it back through W2.

payload.caption: Forward makes a guess. Backward sends the error back the same way, one layer at a time.

payload.title: Why out * (1 - out)
payload.body: It's sigmoid's slope, σ(1 − σ). The chain rule multiplies it in wherever the signal went through a sigmoid.

payload.caption: Type this here

payload.title: Hint
payload.body: Sigmoid's slope is out * (1 - out). Multiply it in at each layer.

payload.title: Train
payload.instructions: Type the training loop, then run python nn.py.
payload.what: A loop that steps every weight downhill 5,000 times
payload.why: Gradient descent: move each weight a little against its gradient, and the loss falls.
payload.code:
lr = 1.0
for epoch in range(5000):
    h, out = forward(X)
    dW2, db2, dW1, db1 = backward(X, y, h, out)
    W2 -= lr * dW2
    b2 -= lr * db2
    W1 -= lr * dW1
    b1 -= lr * db1
    loss = np.mean((out - y) ** 2)
    if epoch % 1000 == 0:
        print(f"epoch {epoch:4d}  loss {loss:.4f}")

payload.title: Loss is stuck at 0.25
payload.body: Your loss hasn't moved in 5,000 epochs. The tutorial's falls below 0.01.
payload.guidingQuestion: If every hidden neuron starts the same, can they ever become different?

payload.title: Loss is stuck at 0.25
payload.body: Start W1 and W2 random, like the lesson. Zeros make every hidden neuron identical.

payload.caption: Start these random, like the lesson

payload.title: Why zeros can't learn
payload.body: All four hidden neurons compute sigmoid(0) = 0.5 and get the same update, so they stay copies. Here nothing moves at all.

payload.caption: With every weight at zero, all four hidden neurons compute 0.5 and get the same update. They stay copies.

payload.title: Why lr = 1.0
payload.body: A tiny network with a smooth loss can take big steps. On real data you would start nearer 0.01.
